title: AI Cannot Replace Human Intuition
excerpt: What Demon Slayer Reveals About Human Strength to Survive in the Age of AI.
content:
What Demon Slayer Reveals About Human Strength to Survive in the Age of AI.

People are terrified of AI.

Not because machines are becoming intelligent.

But because humans are beginning to question
what makes them valuable.

That’s why people are terrified of “AI unemployment.”

So then — what is left for humans?

What kind of leader will survive in this new era?

AI dominates rationality.

It processes massive amounts of past data,
builds logical structures,
and predicts the future that is statistically most likely to happen.

But there are things AI cannot do.

It cannot read what lies beneath meaning. It cannot sense timing.

It cannot perceive possibilities before they fully take shape.

AI generates answers.

But human intuition finds what exists beyond the question itself.

AI predicts the future based on the past. What AI sees is probability.

But human intuition works differently. It perceives hidden potential.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

Both Intuition and Sensation are categorised in the irrational function.

That is why Kagaya and Amane Ubuyashiki matters now more than ever.

In Demon Slayer, he makes one of the most important decisions in the entire story without any rational explanation.

He decides the timing of the final battle.

Why now? When asked, he simply says:

“Muzan will come.
Within the next few days.
I just intuit it.”

This is not irrationality. It is intuition.

In Jungian psychology, intuition is called an “irrational function.”

Not because it lacks logic.

But because it does not depend on measurable data.
It reads messages from the unconscious.

How strongly does your intuition work?

Are you guided mainly by logic (Thinking)?

Or are you guided by something you still cannot fully put into words — intuition, sensation, or another inner signal?

Understanding this difference
is one of the first steps to surviving the age of AI.

In the next article, I will begin with a simple question:

Are you psychologically more guided by intuition, or by sensation?

This is the first step of self-analysis.

If “intuition” is dominant,
dreams may become one of your strongest channels for receiving inner messages for the future orientation.

If “sensation” is dominant,
your strength may appear through another kind of perception:
the body, the senses, images, textures, sounds,
or the atmosphere of the present moment.

And beyond that, there is another essential ability for the coming era:

the ability to connect and collaborate
with people who are completely different from yourself.

We will explore more about this issue in the next articles.
